full_title: PEOPLE OF THE PHILIPPINES, PLAINTIFF-APPELLEE, VS. XXX258643, ACCUSED-APPELLANT.
subject: Criminal Law
syllabus_topic: III. The Revised Penal Code – Book Two > H. Title VIII – Crimes Against Persons
topics: Rape by force: refusing to heed the victim's resistance is force
Resistance need not be tenacious nor made before the act (Art. 266-D)
Acts of lasciviousness against a minor: RA 7610, Sec. 5(b) vs. Art. 336 RPC (Gramatica)
Civil indemnity and damages for acts of lasciviousness against a minor
doctrine:
**Refusing to heed the victim's expression of resistance constitutes force, whether the resistance is made prior to, at the beginning of, or in the middle of the sexual act.** Sexual congress with a person who expressed resistance by words (telling the accused to stop) or deeds (trying to stand up while being held down) is rape under Article 266-A of the RPC. Resistance need not be tenacious: Article 266-D accepts "[a]ny physical overt act manifesting resistance against the act of rape in any degree" as evidence, and the En Banc rule in *People v. Dulay* that tenacious resistance is not required was not overturned by *People v. Tionloc* and *People v. Cubay*. Force need not be irresistible, and the age gap between an adult offender and a minor victim may place the offender in a position to force his will. "It is the job of this Court to say what the law is; not how and when victims should resist sexual acts."

The **sweetheart theory** (reiterated) is an admission of carnal knowledge. The accused must prove by substantial evidence not only that he and the victim were lovers, but that she consented to the sexual act. A love affair does not justify rape.

Applying *Gramatica v. People* and *People v. XXX266039* (En Banc, 2025), lascivious conduct against a minor aged 12 to below 18 falls under **Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610 only if the child was "subjected to sexual abuse"**: the child indulged or engaged in the conduct (consented, though the consent is defective under the law), or was convinced, cajoled, or prevailed upon to take part because of the adult's "employment, use, persuasion, inducement, enticement or coercion." Without such proof, the crime is **acts of lasciviousness under Article 336 of the RPC**. Because the resulting penalty was significantly lower than under RA No. 7610, the Court awarded PHP 75,000.00 each as civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages.
facts:
Accused-appellant XXX, then 24 and a member of the Citizen Armed Force Geographical Unit (CAFGU) at a patrol base in Ligao City, Albay, was charged in four Informations involving AAA, then 14 (born January 21, 2003), whose father BBB was also assigned at the base. Criminal Case Nos. 8159, 8160, and 8161 charged rape through force, threat, and intimidation on December 16, 21, and 26, 2016. Criminal Case No. 8162 charged sexual abuse under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610, through influence and coercion, on December 28, 2016.

AAA testified that on December 16, XXX pushed her onto a bamboo bed and pulled down her shorts and underwear while she tried to pull them up. He then inserted his penis into her vagina while she tried to push him away; she told him to stop because her father was calling her, but he continued. On December 21, at an abandoned house, he made her bend over and had intercourse with her while holding her back as she tried to stand; she told him to stop, but he would not listen until he ejaculated. On December 26, he dragged her into a hut and, ignoring her pleas, had intercourse with her while pushing down on her back as she tried to stand. On December 28, he dragged and carried her to a hut, removed her shorts and underwear, and placed her legs on his shoulders. He tried to insert his penis but failed because she tried to stand up, and he stopped when they heard her father's motorcycle. The abuse came to light in January 2017. XXX claimed they were sweethearts and that they only talked during those meetings.

In its Joint Judgment dated August 2, 2018, the RTC convicted XXX of rape in Criminal Case No. 8159, with reclusion perpetua and PHP 75,000.00 each as civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages. Finding no similar allegation that the December 21, 26, and 28 incidents were attended by force, restraint, or intimidation, it convicted him of sexual abuse under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610 in Criminal Case Nos. 8160 to 8162. In its Decision dated July 17, 2020 (CA-G.R. CR-HC No. 11692), the CA affirmed but reduced the awards in Criminal Case Nos. 8160 to 8162 to PHP 20,000.00 civil indemnity, PHP 15,000.00 moral damages, and PHP 15,000.00 exemplary damages each. XXX appealed.
issues: Whether accused-appellant was correctly convicted of rape in Criminal Case No. 8159 despite his sweetheart theory and his claims about AAA's behavior after the incident.
Whether the CA correctly affirmed accused-appellant's conviction for sexual abuse under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610, instead of rape, in Criminal Case Nos. 8160 and 8161.
Whether accused-appellant was correctly convicted of sexual abuse under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610 in Criminal Case No. 8162, and what civil liability attaches.
ruling:
**1. Yes, the rape conviction in Criminal Case No. 8159 stands.** AAA's positive and categorical testimony established carnal knowledge through force: he pushed her onto the bed and forcibly pulled down her clothes, and she tried to push him away. The sweetheart theory effectively admits carnal knowledge and places on the accused the burden of proving the relationship by substantial evidence, and also that the victim consented to sexual relations. Apart from self-serving statements, he proved no relationship. In any case, "a 'love affair' does not justify rape, for the beloved cannot be sexually violated against her will." His theory that the charge was filed to save the family's honor was speculation; the gravamen of rape is sexual intercourse without consent. "Love is not a license for lust."

**2. No, he is guilty of rape, not sexual abuse, in Criminal Case Nos. 8160 and 8161.** The RTC's own findings showed that AAA told him to stop and tried to stand up while he held or pushed down her back. These are expressions of resistance. Citing *People v. Quintos*, sexual congress with a person who expressed resistance by words or deeds constitutes force; thus **"the mere act of refusing to heed the victim's expression of resistance already constitutes force."** Since *People v. Momo* (1931), force need not be irresistible. The old rule that resistance must be "manifested and tenacious" (*Cabading*, *Amogis*) was rejected by the Court En Banc in *People v. Dulay* (2002), consistent with Article 266-D, which accepts resistance "in any degree" and contemplates victims who could not resist at all. *Tionloc* and *Cubay* revived the old rule, and *Tionloc* even required resistance before consummation, but they "did not overturn the rule on resistance in Dulay," and *Nocido* reaffirmed that tenacious resistance is unnecessary. **"Whether the resistance is made prior to, at the beginning of, or in the middle of the sexual act, it is resistance just the same."** Citing *People v. Caballo*, the age disparity (24 vs. 14) placed him in a stronger position, and he had to drag and carry her on more than one occasion.

**3. No, the crime in Criminal Case No. 8162 is acts of lasciviousness under Article 336 of the RPC.** On December 28 there was no sexual intercourse; he only removed AAA's underwear and placed her legs on his shoulders before they heard her father's motorcycle. Under *Gramatica v. People* and *People v. XXX266039*, RA No. 7610 applies only where the minor is subjected to sexual abuse, that is, she indulged or engaged in (consented, albeit defectively) or was convinced, cajoled, or prevailed upon to take part in the lascivious conduct due to the adult's "employment, use, persuasion, inducement, enticement or coercion." There was no such proof, so he is liable under Article 336. *People v. Tulagan* fixed PHP 20,000.00 each in damages for acts of lasciviousness against a victim of legal age. Following *XXX266039*, however, and **because the penalty for acts of lasciviousness is significantly lower than the penalty under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610, the Court found PHP 75,000.00 each as civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages justified.**
disposition: The appeal was DISMISSED, and the CA Decision dated July 17, 2020 in CA-G.R. CR-HC No. 11692 was AFFIRMED with MODIFICATION. In Criminal Case Nos. 8159, 8160, and 8161, accused-appellant was found GUILTY of three counts of rape and sentenced to reclusion perpetua for each count, and ordered to pay AAA PHP 75,000.00 each as civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages per count. In Criminal Case No. 8162, he was found GUILTY of acts of lasciviousness under Article 336 of the RPC and sentenced to an indeterminate penalty of six months of arresto mayor, as minimum, to four years and two months of prision correccional, as maximum, and ordered to pay PHP 75,000.00 each as civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages. All amounts earn 6% interest per annum from finality until fully paid.

bar_questions.q: Carla, 19, went with Bert into his room. She said nothing when Bert undressed her and began having sexual intercourse with her. Shortly after he started, Carla said, "Stop, I don't want this," and tried to get up, but Bert held her down by the shoulders and continued until he ejaculated. Charged with rape, Bert argues that Carla did not resist before the intercourse began and that her words and her attempt to get up in the middle of the act fall short of the tenacious resistance the law requires. Is Bert guilty of rape?

alac.answer: Yes. Bert is guilty of rape through force, because he refused to heed Carla's expression of resistance.
alac.legal_basis: Under Article 266-A(1)(a) of the RPC, rape is committed by a man who has carnal knowledge of a woman through force, threat, or intimidation. Sexual congress with a person who expressed resistance by words or deeds constitutes force, and "the mere act of refusing to heed the victim's expression of resistance already constitutes force." Resistance need not be tenacious (People v. Dulay, En Banc), and Article 266-D accepts any physical overt act manifesting resistance "in any degree" as evidence. "Whether the resistance is made prior to, at the beginning of, or in the middle of the sexual act, it is resistance just the same." (People v. XXX258643, G.R. No. 258643, February 9, 2026)
alac.application: Carla expressed resistance both by words ("Stop, I don't want this") and by deed (trying to get up). Bert disregarded both and held her down to continue the act. That refusal to heed her resistance is the force that makes the act rape. Her silence at the start does not matter: resistance offered in the middle of the act is still resistance. The law also does not require it to be tenacious. The contrary view in Tionloc, that resistance must come before consummation, did not overturn the En Banc rule in Dulay.

bar_questions.q: Dindo, 22, is charged with raping Ella, 17. He admits having sexual intercourse with her but says they were sweethearts. He presents love letters and photographs of them together, which Ella admits are authentic. Ella testified that on the night in question she told Dindo she did not want to have sex and tried to push him away, but he was too strong and continued. Will Dindo's sweetheart defense prosper?

alac.answer: No. Even if the relationship is proved, the sweetheart defense fails because there is no proof that Ella consented to the sexual act.
alac.legal_basis: The sweetheart theory is an admission of carnal knowledge and places on the accused the burden of proving the relationship by substantial evidence. Because it rests on the premise that the sexual act was consensual, it requires proof not only that the accused and the victim were lovers but also that the victim consented to the sexual relations. "[A] 'love affair' does not justify rape, for the beloved cannot be sexually violated against her will." The gravamen of rape is sexual intercourse without consent. (People v. XXX258643, G.R. No. 258643, February 9, 2026)
alac.application: Dindo's letters and photographs prove only that he and Ella were sweethearts. They do not prove that she agreed to have sex that night. Her testimony that she said no and tried to push him away shows lack of consent. His refusal to heed that resistance is the force that makes it rape. His admission of intercourse, combined with proof of non-consent, supports conviction.
alac.conclusion: The sweetheart defense will not prosper, and Dindo may be convicted of rape.

bar_questions.q: Fred, 25, dragged Gina, 15, into a hut, laid her on a bed, removed her shorts, and touched her private parts against her will until they were interrupted. There was no sexual intercourse. Fred was charged with lascivious conduct under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610. The evidence shows that Fred acted through force; nothing shows that Gina went along with the acts or that Fred persuaded, induced, enticed, or cajoled her into taking part. (a) Of what crime may Fred be held liable? (b) What civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages may be awarded?

alac.answer: (a) Fred is liable for acts of lasciviousness under Article 336 of the RPC, not under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610. (b) PHP 75,000.00 each as civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages may be awarded, with 6% interest per annum from finality.
alac.legal_basis: Not all acts of lasciviousness against minors aged 12 to below 18 are prosecuted under RA No. 7610. Section 5(b) applies only to minors "subjected to sexual abuse": those who indulge or engage in, that is, consent (albeit defectively) to, the lascivious conduct, or who are convinced, cajoled, or prevailed upon to take part due to the adult's "employment, use, persuasion, inducement, enticement or coercion" (Gramatica v. People, En Banc, 2025). Absent such proof, the crime is acts of lasciviousness under Article 336 of the RPC. Applying this rule, the Court in People v. XXX258643 (G.R. No. 258643, February 9, 2026) convicted the accused of acts of lasciviousness. It awarded PHP 75,000.00 each in damages, more than the PHP 20,000.00 set in Tulagan for adult victims, because the penalty imposed was significantly lower than that under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610.
alac.application: (a) Gina is 15, but there is no proof that she indulged or engaged in the conduct or was induced or cajoled into taking part; Fred simply forced himself on her. The case therefore does not fall under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610, and Fred is liable for acts of lasciviousness under Article 336. (b) As in People v. XXX258643, the victim is a minor and the penalty under Article 336 is much lower than what Section 5(b) would have carried, so PHP 75,000.00 each in civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages is justified.
alac.conclusion: Fred is liable for acts of lasciviousness under Article 336 of the RPC and may be ordered to pay PHP 75,000.00 each as civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages.

notes: Only accused-appellant appealed, yet the Court convicted him of rape (instead of sexual abuse under Section 5(b) of RA No. 7610) in Criminal Case Nos. 8160 and 8161, where the Informations had charged rape; the main opinion does not separately discuss the rule that an appeal in a criminal case opens the whole case for review. On the December 28 incident (attempted insertion that failed), the Court ruled that the crime was acts of lasciviousness because there was no sexual intercourse; it did not discuss attempted rape. Apparent typographical errors in the text: the opening paragraph refers to sexual abuse under "Republic Act No. 7160" (should be 7610), and the CA's summary of the defense version dates one incident "December 28, 2017" (the other dates are in 2016). The caption anonymizes the accused as XXX258643; the body calls him XXX.
